paragraph: Lyndhurst's core is single-family, 37 sales over six months at a median of $600,000, with a sale-to-list ratio of 1.008 and a median of 19 days on market. Nearly 60 percent sold above asking, but the ratio says those overages are small. Competitive but not frenzied, and correctly priced homes are moving quickly. The range runs from $453,000 to $1,089,000, so the median is the better guide than either end. Multi-family is the tier where sellers are dictating terms, 21 sales at a median of $850,000, a 1.048 ratio and 71 percent selling above list. That is investor and owner-occupant demand competing for the same two-family stock, and buyers here should expect to bid over ask. Condos and townhouses are thin, 9 sales at a median of $415,000 with 18 days on market, enough activity to establish a price point but not enough to read much into month to month. On seasonality, monthly counts are small, but July brought the highest single-family volume of the period at 9 closings and a median of $640,000, which tracks the usual Bergen County summer peak. If the normal pattern holds, expect closings and medians to ease through fall. If you're weighing tiers, the question is whether you want the space and yard of a single-family, the rental income of a two-family, or the low-maintenance setup of a condo.
